examples.html: Center for Freight and Logistics Efficiency with Electrified and Automated Trucking (FLEET)

og.title: Center for Freight and Logistics Efficiency with Electrified and Automated Trucking (FLEET)
og.description: The Center for Freight and Logistics Efficiency with Electrified and Automated Trucking brings industry and academia together to solve some of the most pressing problems facing the trucking industry and transportation today. Commercial trucking is a critical sector, supporting the supply chains of many other sectors, and moves most of the products consumed in the U.S., yet it remains one of the least automated, most labor-intensive modes of transport. Driving a commercial truck is currently the seventh most dangerous profession, with truckers suffering almost 20% of all U.S. workplace deaths. Meanwhile, transit bus systems face severe economic challenges in providing public transportation.FLEET's vision is to converge and apply knowledge in emerging technologies in connected, electrified, and automated commercial vehicles and logistics networks for efficient, safe, agile, and sustainable mobility for the benefit of society. FLEET will focus on the challenges faced by agencies managing commercial fleets including trucking, transit, rail, port, and others. By bringing together a coalition of private and public sector stakeholders and academic institutions, FLEET aims to conduct transdisciplinary research on electrified truck powertrains, highly automated vehicle/road transportation, real-time truck platooning and caravanning technology, public transit vehicles, smart infrastructure, and supply-chain network models. The ultimate goal is to drive innovation and facilitate the widespread adoption of electric and automated commercial vehicles for sustainable freight and public transportation in North America and worldwide.

checks.label: HTTPS (required for service workers)
checks.why: HTTPS is required for service workers and most install prompts.

checks.label: Web app manifest declared
checks.why: A web app manifest is required for installability and controls how the app appears when launched.

checks.label: Service worker registered
checks.why: A service worker is what makes offline access, caching, and background sync possible.

checks.label: Theme color declared
checks.why: Theme color controls the browser chrome/status-bar color when the site is installed or bookmarked.

checks.label: Apple touch icon (iOS/bookmark icon)
checks.why: iOS uses this icon for home-screen bookmarks and "Add to Home Screen" — without it the icon falls back to a screenshot.

checks.label: Manifest fetched and parsed successfully
checks.why: A manifest that fails to parse cannot drive installability or launch behavior even if the link is present.

checks.label: Manifest declares a maskable icon
checks.why: A maskable icon lets the OS safely crop/mask the app icon on different device shapes without clipping content.

checks.label: Service worker is active (not just registered)
checks.why: An active service worker (not just registered) is what actually intercepts requests and serves cached content.

checks.label: Service worker controls this page load
checks.why: A controlling service worker means THIS page load is being served/intercepted, not just a future one.

checks.label: Meets basic installability criteria
checks.evidence: no readable web app manifest; no service worker registered
checks.why: Determines whether the browser can realistically offer "Add to Home Screen" / install, based on manifest + service worker + HTTPS together.
